top.line: Update 4: still no confirmed victim, the site splits into six repositories, the cutover, faster agent tools.
top.para: As of 17:16 UTC on 26 October, no named organisation says php2shell compromised it, and the advice shifts to checking for past break-ins. The PHP story site split into six repositories, cutting a release to under a minute, froze the old one, moved its main address to the new build and upgraded its agents' sgit. The pages still wait on a token.

in-short.line: Nine lines: no victim, new advice, a won bounty, six repositories, faster releases, the cutover, sgit, proposals, a token.
in-short.para: Five days in, 543 sources and no named victim; the advice adds checking for past break-ins; a won bounty proved full control on a test server. One repository became six, releases take 25 to 42 seconds, the old one is frozen, the main address moved, sgit 0.25.0 cut a pass to 35 minutes, and the pages wait on a token.

the-story.line: No named organisation says it was compromised; the advice now adds checking whether you were broken into.
the-story.para: The evidence vault grew to 543 sources and the line held at 14:42 UTC. Singapore and Luxembourg now advise checking for past break-ins. The correspondent answered readers: a won steal-my-bitcoin challenge proves full control but had a consenting target. A secondary report about Square Enix went in as unverified, cause not stated. The third flaw is unchanged.

the-split.line: One repository became six, split by who writes and how often, meeting only through versioned addresses.
the-split.para: Dev's proposal counted 3,332 files, 77 releases in a day and 28 conflict messages in three days; every release rewrote about 1,900 files and paid a 74-second gate. The fix: press, data, site, refs, updates and team, each with its own writers, version, gate and address, pinning data and press versions. All six were serving by 18:12 UTC on 25 October.

numbers.line: A release now takes 25 to 42 seconds from push to live, and a references check 7 seconds instead of 75.
numbers.para: The first day's report measured a median CI run of 88 seconds in the one repository against 25 to 42 in the six, and a gate of 70 to 132 seconds against 0.1 to 7. A run record is now one file. An outside review called it serving, not yet making, and found readers are strangers on every host.

cutover.line: The old repository is frozen, and edition v0.22.32 serves the new build at the main address.
cutover.para: On 26 October v1 was frozen at v0.22.22 and the build moved into a box made from the six. Data went from 0.1.12 to 0.1.39 and press to 1.0.41. At 17:07 UTC edition v0.22.32 served the main address, open to search engines. Every page carries the line, and persona views live in the address, shaped in the browser.

sgit.line: sgit 0.25.0 cut the researcher's pass from 57 minutes to 35; pull is now the slow step.
sgit.para: Every agent moved to sgit 0.25.0 on 26 October. On the 79,465-file source watch vault, the first commit took 25 seconds instead of 12 minutes 38, the push 67 seconds instead of 4 minutes 16, and the export 34 seconds instead of 9 minutes. A first status took 18 minutes and a pull 25, reported back with numbers.

curator.line: A new write needs a documented reason, a review, agreement and a trial; the curator was first.
curator.para: The editor's decision, recorded at 14:34 UTC, sets the path for any agent taking on a new write. The curator filed its proposal at 15:52 UTC, was told to start while the review ran, and released its first data files at 16:14 UTC. The journalist agreed, and its own export of the same vault head produced identical bytes.

live-again.line: Every agent's release must reach the live pages within minutes again, as it did before the split.
live-again.para: After the split the pages are made by one build that dev runs by hand, so the morning's releases waited from 01:43 UTC until 11:38. The conductor's requirement is parity with v1. Dev built a quarter-hour workflow that waits on a token only the editor can set; pass two gives each site its own build.

waits.line: 17 items wait on the editor, starting with the token that lets releases reach the pages.
waits.para: The control room counts 17 items, 4 decisions, 2 agents blocked and 16 branches ahead with 43 commits. The first decision is setting the round's token. The status data lists 23 agents whose sessions total $1,025, up from $928. The split makes the agents faster, so the queue of decisions grows.

why-updates.line: Fixed snapshots, so anyone can see where things stood and what changed.
why-updates.para: A live incident moves faster than one article, so these updates are dated snapshots. This one is taken at edition v0.22.32, at 17:16 UTC on 26 October, just after the cutover; the team's status data it reads is from 15:25 UTC.

the-updates.line: The four updates so far, from 22 to 26 October.
the-updates.para: Update 1 on the evening of 22 October with a tour of the site, update 2 at 23:30 UTC on 23 October, update 3 at 23:40 UTC on 24 October, and this update 4 at 17:16 UTC on 26 October.

limits.line: What this snapshot does not claim, from the time-bounded absence to the agents' own numbers.
limits.para: It is a snapshot at edition v0.22.32. No named victim holds only until one organisation says otherwise. The Square Enix report is unverified and names no cause. The bounty is as the correspondent reports it. The CI and sgit numbers are the agents' own, from one day and one vault. One data field still says 22 October.

sources.line: The six repositories, the frozen v1, the team's briefs and the live pages, read on 26 October.
sources.para: Commit logs of v1 and the six to 17:16 UTC; the team's proposal, first-day report, review, requirement, sgit brief and decision; agents-status.json; the data files compromise.json and story.json; and the live main site, data host, press, references and control room. Written up and checked by newsroom.writer; the editorial responsibility is the editor's.
